description:
Apply a unified diff (git apply compatible) to one or more files, all-or-nothing. Every file is validated in memory before anything is written; a failing hunk rolls every file back from an automatic checkpoint, like edit_batch. dry_run=true validates and reports without writing.
Use when: a change arrives as a diff (git diff, a patch file, another tool's output) and must land completely or not at all — files created, modified, deleted or renamed.
Avoid when: you have no diff (edit_file/edit_batch) or only need a new file (write_file). Not for directories or symbolic links.
Output: dry_run: files[] {action, relative_path, hunks, bytes} plus added/modified/deleted/renamed counts; nothing is written. success: same list plus sha256_after per file. Failure: nothing is changed; data carries rollback_succeeded and, for a mismatching hunk, nearest_context lines for the file and hunk that failed.

dry_run.description: true validates the patch against the current files and reports what would change, writing nothing (default false).

expected_sha256.description: Optional map of workspace-relative path -> hex SHA-256; the patch is refused if a file changed since it was read. Keys must be paths the patch touches.

patch.description: Unified diff. Multiple files supported: each section starts with 'diff --git a/old b/new' or '--- a/old' + '+++ b/new' ('/dev/null' for created/deleted files).
